questions.title: Linear Search Index
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int linear_search(int arr[], int n, int target)

It must return the FIRST 0-based index whose element equals target, or -1 when absent.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: target.

Output Format:
One line with the index or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, |value|, |target| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Binary Search Index
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int binary_search(int arr[], int n, int target)

The array is sorted ascending with DISTINCT values. It must return the 0-based index of target, or -1 when absent.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n sorted distinct integers. Line 3: target.

Output Format:
One line with the index or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, |value|, |target| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Missing Token Number
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int missing_token(int arr[], int m)

The register holds m distinct token numbers taken from 1..m+1 with exactly one number missing (order not guaranteed). It must return the missing number.

Line 1: m. Line 2: m distinct integers from 1..m+1 (one is missing).

Output Format:
One line with the missing number.

questions.title: Closest Temperature Reading
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int closest_value(int arr[], int n, int target)

It must return the array value minimising |value - target|; when two values tie, return the smaller one.

Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: target.

One line with the closest value.

1 <= n <= 10000, |value|, |target| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Locker Assignment Lookup
questions.description:
A gym maps member IDs to lockers in arrival order. Given a member ID, report the 1-based locker number holding that ID, or -1 when the member has no locker.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int locker_for(int ids[], int n, int member)

It must return the 1-based position of member in ids, or -1 when absent.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated member IDs. Line 3: the member to find.

Output Format:
One line with the 1-based locker number or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, 1 <= value <= 1000000000

questions.title: Dictionary Shelf Binary Lookup
questions.description:
A library keeps catalogue codes on sorted distinct shelves. Binary search probes one shelf per step; the metrics page wants the number of PROBES a successful lookup takes (or -1 when the code is absent).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int binary_probes(int arr[], int n, int target)

Run a standard binary search (lo = 0, hi = n - 1, mid = (lo + hi) / 2); each mid examination counts as one probe. Return the probe count when found, else -1.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n sorted distinct integers. Line 3: target.

Output Format:
One line with the probe count or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, |value|, |target| <= 1000000000

Output Format:
One line with the seat count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, 1 <= value, p <= 1000000000

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n sorted integers. Line 3: target.

Output Format:
One line with the leftmost index or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, |value|, |target| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Search Insert Position
questions.description:
A sorted distinct roster should receive a new value without breaking the order. Report the 0-based index where the value already sits, or the index where it should be inserted.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int insert_position(int arr[], int n, int target)

questions.title: Bitonic Peak Index

questions.title: Floor and Ceiling Report
questions.description:
A pricing tool reports, for a query x over a sorted distinct list: the FLOOR (largest value <= x, -1 when none) and the CEILING (smallest value >= x, -1 when none).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void floor_ceil(int arr[], int n, int x, int *floor, int *ceil)

It must store both results. The harness prints them.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n sorted distinct integers. Line 3: x.

Output Format:
One line with the floor, then the ceiling, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, |value|, |x| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Rotated Array Search
questions.description:
A sorted distinct list was rotated left by an unknown amount. Binary search still works with a twist: identify which half is sorted, then keep only the half that can contain the target.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int rotated_search(int arr[], int n, int target)

It must return the 0-based index of target, or -1 when absent.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n distinct integers (rotated ascending order). Line 3: target.

Output Format:
One line with the index or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, |value|, |target| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Bounds of the Target Block

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n sorted integers. Line 3: target.

Output Format:
One line with first, last and count, space-separated.

Line 1: n. Line 2: n distinct integers (rotated ascending order).

Output Format:
One line with the minimum value.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Integer Square Root by Halving
questions.description:
A chip lacks a floating-point unit, so the floor of sqrt(x) is computed with a binary search over candidate answers. Math functions are forbidden.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int int_sqrt(int x)

It must return the largest integer r with r * r <= x (0 when x = 0). Do not call sqrt or include math.h.

Input Format:
One line with x.

Output Format:
One line with the integer square root.

Constraints:
0 <= x <= 2000000000

questions.title: Kth Missing Positive

    int kth_missing(int arr[], int n, int k)

Input Format:

Output Format:

Constraints:
